source_policy.preservation_rule: Preserve source concepts, equations, examples, distinctions, historical attributions, references, and framing; do not silently substitute external content.

relationship_model.principle: Relationships are first-class semantic objects. A relationship preserves direction, mechanism, conditions, mathematical form, effect, inverse/converse, frame dependence, scope, source provenance, semantic role, and linked equations.

key_relationships.force_to_acceleration: net force → acceleration via F=dp/dt and, for constant mass, F=ma. Direction and magnitude are explicitly retained.
key_relationships.acceleration_to_velocity: acceleration → velocity change via Δv=∫a dt; inverse differential relation a=dv/dt.
key_relationships.velocity_to_acceleration: velocity → acceleration via time derivative dv/dt.
key_relationships.position_to_acceleration: position → acceleration via second derivative d²x/dt².
key_relationships.jerk_to_acceleration: jerk → acceleration change via Δa=∫j dt.
key_relationships.speed_direction_to_acceleration: speed change → tangential acceleration; direction change → normal acceleration.
key_relationships.circular_motion: constant speed + changing velocity direction → centripetal acceleration.
key_relationships.relativity: Newtonian acceleration is a low-speed approximation; high-speed behavior is revised by special relativity, while GR links gravity and inertial acceleration locally.

source_claims.title: Definition
source_claims.claim: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity and a vector quantity.

source_claims.title: Average acceleration
source_claims.claim: Average acceleration is Δv/Δt.

source_claims.title: Instantaneous acceleration
source_claims.claim: Instantaneous acceleration is dv/dt and d²x/dt².

source_claims.title: Integral hierarchy
source_claims.claim: Integrating acceleration gives velocity change; integrating jerk gives acceleration change.

source_claims.title: Force relation
source_claims.claim: Net force produces net acceleration; magnitude is proportional to force and inversely proportional to mass.

source_claims.title: Units
source_claims.claim: Acceleration has dimensions L T^-2 and SI unit m/s².

source_claims.title: Frames
source_claims.claim: Proper acceleration is measured by accelerometer; accelerating frames use fictitious force.

source_claims.title: Constant mass Newtonian law
source_claims.claim: F=ma and a=F/m apply to center-of-mass acceleration for constant mass in classical mechanics.

source_claims.title: Vehicle examples
source_claims.claim: Speeding, turning and slowing illustrate tangential, radial and opposite-velocity acceleration.

source_claims.title: Curved path
source_claims.claim: Acceleration decomposes into tangential and normal components.

source_claims.title: Frenet
source_claims.claim: Frenet–Serret formulas describe local curve geometry.

source_claims.title: Uniform acceleration
source_claims.claim: Equal velocity changes occur in equal time intervals.

source_claims.title: Free fall
source_claims.claim: Free fall without resistance has acceleration governed by g; Fg=mg.

source_claims.title: Kinematic equations
source_claims.claim: Constant acceleration yields standard x(t), v(t), v² relations and parabolic projectile motion.

source_claims.title: Circular motion
source_claims.claim: Constant-speed circular motion still has inward acceleration.

source_claims.title: Angular relations
source_claims.claim: v=ωr, a_c=−ω²r, a_t=rα and α=ωdot.

source_claims.title: Coordinates
source_claims.claim: Acceleration decomposes into Cartesian components and magnitudes.

source_claims.title: Special relativity
source_claims.claim: Newtonian mechanics is a low-speed approximation; acceleration from a given force decreases toward light speed.

source_claims.title: General relativity
source_claims.claim: Gravity and inertial acceleration can be locally indistinguishable.

source_claims.title: Conversions
source_claims.claim: Gal, ft/s², m/s² and g0 conversions are listed.

misconceptions_and_corrections.correction: Circular motion can maintain constant speed while velocity direction changes, producing centripetal acceleration.
Deceleration is acceleration antiparallel to velocity.

misconceptions_and_corrections.misconception: Force and acceleration are the same quantity
misconceptions_and_corrections.correction: They are distinct; F=ma relates them under stated assumptions.
Normal acceleration can change direction with no speed change.

misconceptions_and_corrections.misconception: Centrifugal force is always a real interaction
misconceptions_and_corrections.correction: The source identifies it as a pseudo force in the rotating frame.

misconceptions_and_corrections.misconception: Gravity and acceleration are always distinguishable
misconceptions_and_corrections.correction: The source invokes local equivalence of gravitational and inertial acceleration.

misconceptions_and_corrections.misconception: Newtonian equations are exact at all speeds
misconceptions_and_corrections.correction: The source states they are a low-speed approximation.

misconceptions_and_corrections.misconception: Average and instantaneous acceleration are always identical
misconceptions_and_corrections.correction: They coincide for uniform acceleration, but their definitions differ.
Changing velocity direction alone is acceleration.

misconceptions_and_corrections.misconception: More mass gives more free-fall acceleration
misconceptions_and_corrections.correction: In the stated idealized relation Fg=mg, g determines free-fall acceleration while mass scales force.

misconceptions_and_corrections.misconception: Centripetal force is a separate fundamental interaction
misconceptions_and_corrections.correction: It is the net inward force required by circular acceleration, not necessarily a new interaction type.
The article explicitly treats it as a vector.
Zero acceleration means velocity is constant, which can include nonzero velocity.

misconceptions_and_corrections.misconception: Fictitious force is an ordinary interaction force
misconceptions_and_corrections.correction: It is introduced by non-inertial frame description.

misconceptions_and_corrections.misconception: Centripetal acceleration is linear in speed
misconceptions_and_corrections.correction: At fixed radius the source gives v² dependence.
Jerk is derivative of acceleration, not force.
